## 1. Reachability — the answer is not what the issue expects

### 1.1 The graph

Fix a marker position `m`. Attention is a per-layer, per-position operation; the only way
information moves between positions is an attention edge. Write `keys(q, type)` for the key set
that a query at `q` reads:

- `full_attention`: `keys(q) = [0, n)`
- `sliding_attention`: `keys(q) = [q-w, q+w] ∩ [0, n)`, `w = 64`

Two different questions can be asked of this graph, and they have **different answers**.

**(A) The ancestral set — "is there any attention path at all?"** Define

```
S_0 = {m};   S_k = ⋃_{q ∈ S_{k-1}} keys(q, layer_type(k-1))
```

`S_k` is the set of positions that can influence position `m` within `k` hops. Because
`layer_type(0) = full_attention` and layer 0 is the *first* layer, `S_1 = [0, n)` — the whole
sequence, at **depth 1**, regardless of distance. The reachability graph of this encoder has
**diameter 1**.

> **Result 1.** For *any* marker position `m` and *any* state token `s`, the minimum number of
> layers for a nonzero attention path is **1**, provided the sequence length is `<= max_position_embeddings`
> (8192). There is no distance-dependent hop count. `[MODELLED]`. Simulated exactly in
> `analyse.py` §1: `|S_k| = 8192` for every `k >= 1`, at `m ∈ {39, 300}`, `n = 8192`.

This refutes one premise the effort was partly built on. `plan.md` §2 and `P1-mechanism.md` say the
marker "aggregates an 8192-token document through 8 cross-document hops". Under the actual layer
pattern it aggregates it through **one** hop that already spans everything, and the other 21 layers
re-mix what that hop produced. That is a materially different bottleneck — and it is the one the
evidence points at (see §2.4).

**(B) The per-hop horizon — "how far can information be pulled per layer?"** This is the model the
issue asks for, and it is the right model *for a single hop*: a query at `m` reading a key at `j`
gets information that `j` itself pooled over `keys(j)` in the previous layer. Composing one mask per
layer from layer 0 and ignoring the fact that layer 0 already reaches everything, the horizon is

```
H_0 = 2w = 128            # m reads [m-64, m+64]; each key carries its own +-64 from the embedding layer
H_t = 2 * H_{t-1}   if layer t is full_attention
H_t = H_{t-1} + w   if layer t is sliding_attention
```

For this exact pattern (global every 3rd layer, starting at 0) the closed form at global layer `3k` is

```
R_0 = 2w = 128 ;   R_k = (8 * 2^k - 1) * w   for k >= 1
```

`[MODELLED]`. Checked against the simulation in `analyse.py` §1 (all 8 global layers, OK).

| `k` | layer `3k` | `R_k` (tokens) | fraction of an 8192 sequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 128 | 1.6 % |
| 1 | 3 | 960 | 12.2 % |
| 2 | 6 | 1984 | 25.1 % |
| 3 | 9 | 4032 | 51.1 % |
| 4 | 12 | 8128 | 99.9 % |
| 5 | 15 | 16320 | 100 % (saturated) |

so the minimum layer index for a token `d` away is

```
L*(d) = 0                                   for d <= 2w = 128
L*(d) = 3 * ceil(log2((d/w + 1) / 8))       for d > 2w
```

`[MODELLED] [DERIVED]`. Instantiated:

| `d = |s-m|` | 128 | 129–960 | 961–1984 | 1985–4032 | 4033–8128 | 8129–8191 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `L*(d)` | 0 | 3 | 6 | 9 | 12 | 15 |

### 1.2 Which one binds

The two answers are only in tension if you treat reachability as a binary. It is not.

- **(A) is the architectural fact**: every token is a depth-1 ancestor of every marker, because
  layer 0 is global. Any claim of the form "the marker cannot reach position 7000" is false, and
  an experiment that would only be informative if it were true is not informative.
- **(B) is the dilution fact**: at distance `d`, the token's contribution must be routed through
  the keys that already pooled a window, and it competes for attention mass against everything
  already in `S_{k-1}`. The cost of distance is *how much of the network has already averaged it
  away*, not whether a path exists.

The operationally useful form of (B) is the **mixing budget**: how many global layers remain to
process a token *after* it first becomes individually addressable. Written as `8 - k`:

| `d` | 1984 | 4032 | 7000 | 8191 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k` (global layers consumed reaching it) | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| **global layers remaining to mix it** | 6 | 5 | **4** | 3 |

`[DERIVED]` from the table above. A marker that must aggregate evidence from ~7000 positions away
first reads that evidence at layer 12 and has four global layers left; at 8191 the first read is
layer 15 and three are left. This, not a hard cutoff, is the quantitative statement of "distance
costs you".

### 1.3 Assumptions, and which one is weakest

| assumption | how sure |
|---|---|
| Sliding layers compose transitively — a path may zig-zag marker → sliding → sliding → global → distant token. | **Certain.** It is just graph composition; each hop re-reads the previous layer's outputs. This is what makes the horizon grow at all. |
| The sliding mask is exactly `|i-j| <= 64` and bidirectional. | **Certain** for this checkpoint — read from `laya/fast.py:53-55`, which explicitly warns that HF's `ModernBertAttention.sliding_window` is `local_attention//2 + 1` and must not be used. |
| The per-hop model is the right *quantitative* model of information transfer. | **Weakest assumption in this section.** It counts hops, not attention mass. §2.3 and the measured evidence below say the binding constraint is softmax normalisation over the whole key set, which no hop count captures. Read §1.1(B) as a *horizon* (how far content can be pulled per layer), never as a probability of recovery. |
| Attention sinks / induction heads do not create shortcuts that beat the graph. | **Unverified.** Nothing here measures attention weights. `P1b` probes the *representation*, which is the right level for this claim; a per-layer attention-mass map would settle it. |

## 2. Mixing capacity — where the long-range edges actually are

### 2.1 Edges, counted exactly

Split the sequence into a **head block** (queries that contain markers) and a **state block** (the
document). Counting cross-document attention edges — (query in head) × (key in state) — summed over
all 22 layers, exactly, for the two configurations that matter `[MODELLED]`:

| configuration | head block | total cross-document edges | from the 8 global layers | from the 14 sliding layers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_len=1024`, shipped | 256 | 1,601,984 | 1,572,864 (**98.2 %**) | 29,120 (1.8 %) |
| `max_len=8192` | 384 | 24,015,296 | 23,986,176 (**99.9 %**) | 29,120 (0.1 %) |

The sliding-layer contribution is **constant at 29,120 edges** — it does not grow with `n`, because
the window is fixed. Per marker, a sliding layer reaches exactly `2w+1 = 129` keys, of which:

| `n` | state block | sliding layer reaches, per marker | as a fraction of the state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 768 | 64 state tokens | 8.33 % |
| 8192 | 7808 | 64 state tokens | 0.82 % |

A full layer reaches 100 % of the state per marker.

### 2.2 The counted distribution, and the issue's framing

The issue asks to make explicit that **only the 8 global layers create direct long-range edges; the
14 sliding layers move information 64 positions per hop.** That is exactly right, and the edge
counts price it: at `n=8192` the globals carry **99.9 %** of the cross-document capacity and the
sliding layers carry **0.1 %**. Total cross-document capacity grows 15× from `n=1024` to `n=8192`,
but *entirely* through the quadratic global layers; the sliding layers are a fixed 29,120-edge
trickle.

There is a subtlety the issue's framing hides, and §1.1(A) is why: the sliding layers are not a
*route* to the document. They are a route to the 64 tokens next to each marker, plus — via
composition — the mechanism by which "how far can a hop pull" doubles at each global layer. Treating
them as "14 hops × 64 = 896 tokens of reach" is the error; the composed horizon at layer 12 is 8128,
because each global layer re-reads a set that already pooled a window. The per-hop number is 64; the
composition over one 3-layer block is ×8; the composition over 4 blocks is ×4096.

### 2.3 What this implies for a marker that must aggregate evidence from ~7000

Three consequences, in decreasing confidence:

1. **The evidence is read late.** At 7000 tokens from the marker, first read is at layer 12 of 22
   (§1.1(B)) — six layers later than evidence at 960 tokens. Only four global layers remain to mix
   it (§1.2).
2. **Everything competes.** Whatever the layer-12 query attends to, it attends to over ~7000
   candidate keys. Under softmax, a single key's weight is at most `1/(number of comparably-scoring
   keys)`; adding filler tokens that score similarly is *directly* destructive. This is the
   mechanism `P1-mechanism.md` labels attention dilution, and `MODELLED` here predicts it should be
   worse than a hop-count model would suggest: the marker's most useful comparison (needle vs
   filler) does not exist — filler has no features the marker was ever trained to suppress.
3. **A direct question, answerable by a cheap probe.** If reachability bound, accuracy would fall
   off as a step function in `L*(d)` — flat within a band, dropping at 129 / 961 / 1985 / 4033 /
   8129. If dilution binds, accuracy falls off smoothly in `n` and in the *amount of similar
   content*, and per §2.2 the fall-off should track the **state block size**, not the absolute
   distance. The measured evidence (§2.4) says: smooth in both, and position matters at constant
   length — i.e. **dilution, not hop count**.

### 2.4 This is consistent with what the lab has already measured

Not my measurement; recorded here because it decides how the rest of this document should be read.
`[MEASURED — other agent]`, reproduced from `findings/P1b-information-location.md` (n=200,
4000-token document, needle at the end) — I did not run this; the artifact is
`experiments/orch-probe-d/results.json`:

| feature | grouped-CV accuracy (needle 4000 tokens away) |
|---|---|
| `marker` (encoder output at the `[MASK]` positions) | **0.820** |
| `cls` | 0.885 |
| `state_max` | 0.895 |
| `random_pos` (control) | 0.440 |
| **shipped head reading those positions** | **0.300** |

and `findings/P1-mechanism.md` (n=20): at fixed 4000-token length, needle at fraction 0.00 scores
0.900 and at fraction 0.25–1.00 scores 0.500–0.600, with nothing truncated.

So: information **does** reach the marker at 0.82, and the head returns 0.30. The bottleneck is the
aggregation path, not the receptive field. That is the same conclusion §1.1(A) reaches from the mask
graph alone, by a completely different route, and it is the strongest single argument for aiming at
the head (H5) rather than at window width (H3). §1.2's "global layers remaining" is then best read
as a *rank* on how hard the head's job is at each distance, not as the cause of the failure.

## 3. Cost model — the prediction, and the miss

### 3.1 The model

Forward-only inference FLOPs (one multiply-accumulate = 2 FLOPs), batch 1, `d=768`, `F=1152`,
`w=64`, `L_full=8`, `L_slide=14`, `head_layers=2`:

```
per encoder layer:   17·n·d²  +  4·n·d·F  +  [ 2·n²·d           full ]
                                            [ 2·n·(2w+1)·d      sliding ]
head (2 layers):     2 · 2·n²·d
```

The `2·n·(2w+1)·d` term is the sliding-layer attention cost — **linear**, `O(n · 128 · d)` as the
issue states. The global-layer term is `O(n² · d)`. `[MODELLED]`.

`analyse.py` §3, `[MODELLED]`:

| `n` | total FLOPs | ratio vs `n=1024` | encoder quadratic share | head quadratic share |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 61 | 1.05e9 | 0.032 | 20.4 % | 1.1 % |
| 1024 | 3.28e10 | 1.000 | 47.9 % | **9.8 %** |
| 2040 | 9.79e10 | 2.981 | 58.5 % | 13.2 % |
| 3006 | 1.88e11 | 5.722 | 63.5 % | 14.8 % |
| 3972 | 3.07e11 | 9.356 | 66.7 % | 15.8 % |
| 5946 | 6.40e11 | 19.496 | 70.4 % | 17.0 % |
| 8192 | 1.16e12 | **35.466** | 72.8 % | 17.7 % |

**Predicted latency ratio `n=8192` vs `n=1024`, fixed model, batch 1: 35.5×.** `[MODELLED]`
(whole table above is `[MODELLED]`).
Encoder only (no head): 32.4×. The head's own two full-self-attention layers are 9.8 % of FLOPs at
`n=1024` and 17.7 % at `n=8192` — **not negligible**, and worth remembering because the head is also
the suspected bottleneck (§2.4): it is the one part of the stack that is both cheap to replace and
already quadratic.

**A bound worth stating.** In this family the ratio `(b·n + c·n²)/(b·n₀ + c·n₀²)` is increasing in
`c >= 0` with supremum `(8192/1024)² = 64×`, approached as the linear term becomes negligible.
So **no assignment of layer types or hidden size can make this model predict 219×** — 219 > 64. Any 219× explanation must be non-FLOPs-proportional. `[MODELLED] [DERIVED]`.

### 3.2 What the upstream artifact actually contains

`[MEASURED upstream]` — every number in the table below. Source
`fork/research/results/long_context_multilingual.json`, device `mps`, n=20 per cell, both `limit`
settings, all rows:

| pad | limit | median input tokens | median latency (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1024 | 61 | 0.017 |
| 0 | 8192 | 61 | 0.016 |
| 1000 | 1024 | 1024 | 0.224 |
| 1000 | 8192 | 1032 | 0.211 |
| 2000 | 1024 | 1024 | 0.198 |
| 2000 | 8192 | 2040 | 0.503 |
| 3000 | 1024 | 1024 | 0.208 |
| 3000 | 8192 | 3006 | 0.895 |
| 4000 | 1024 | 1024 | 0.216 |
| 4000 | 8192 | 3972 | 1.707 |
| 5000 | 1024 | 1024 | 0.262 |
| 5000 | 8192 | 4938 | 2.586 |
| 6000 | 1024 | 1024 | 0.253 |
| 6000 | 8192 | 5946 | 3.505 |
| 7000 | 1024 | 1024 | 0.264 |
| 7000 | 8192 | 6912 | 4.503 |

### 3.3 The headline comparison, normalised

The issue quotes 0.016 s → 3.507 s = **219×**, and warns the input grew too. Correcting two things:

- **The 3.507 s row is `median_input_tokens = 5946`, not 8192.** The `limit=8192` row at `pad=6000`
  delivers 5946 tokens; the model's FLOPs for `n=5946` are only 55 % of the FLOPs for `n=8192`.
- **`limit=1024` truncates the padded request to exactly 1024 tokens**, so the flat 0.198–0.264 s
  across pad 2000–7000 is a flat *cost* at a constant 1024-token input, and the `pad=0` row (61
  tokens) is a 17× smaller input.

| comparison | measured | modelled (FLOPs) | measured / modelled |
|---|---|---|---|
| raw headline: 61 tok → 5946 tok | 219.06× | 607.47× | 0.36 (model over-predicts **2.77×**) |
| **8192 vs 1024** (the issue's stated question) | not measurable — see below | **35.47×** | — |
| 5946 vs 1024, matched input lengths | 19.50× | 19.50× | 1.00 (same n → same FLOPs) |

The "8192 vs 1024" ratio cannot be read off the artifact, because no run in it processed 8192
tokens. The nearest honest substitutes:

**(a) Normalise the input growth.** Put both endpoints at the same input length by scaling the
5946-token latency back to 1024 tokens, and compare against the `limit=1024` run at 1024 tokens:
`(3.505 × 1024/5946) / 0.224 = 2.70×`. The model says the same pair should differ by
`FLOPs(5946)/FLOPs(1024) = 19.50×`. **The model over-predicts by 7.2×.** `[DERIVED]` from
`[MEASURED upstream]` + `[MODELLED]` FLOPs.

**(b) Matched-input pairs, which is the clean version of the same test.** For each pad, compare the
`limit=1024` run against the `limit=8192` run, per-token normalised (multiply the large-`n` latency
by `n₁₀₂₄/n₈₁₉₂`). This removes input growth exactly, at the cost of assuming latency is
approximately `n`-linear over a small range:

| `n` (8192-limit run) | per-token-normalised measured ratio | modelled ratio | measured / modelled |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2040 | 1.275 | 2.962 | 0.43 |
| 3006 | 1.466 | 5.722 | 0.26 |
| 3972 | 2.037 | 9.356 | 0.22 |
| 4938 | 2.047 | 13.863 | 0.15 |
| 5946 | 2.386 | 19.496 | 0.12 |
| 6912 | 2.527 | 25.786 | 0.10 |

**Verdict: the cost model does not match, and the miss is large — 2.4× to 10×, growing with `n`.**
`[MODELLED]` vs `[MEASURED upstream]`. This is a finding, not a failure. Three separable causes,
in order of how much of the gap they explain:

1. **A constant term the model does not have.** A pure-FLOPs model is a homogeneous function of
   `n`; the measured latency is not. Fitting `lat(n) = F + a·n^p` to the eight `limit=8192` medians
   gives **`F = 0.010 s`, `a = 5.575e-07`, `p = 1.800`, RMSE = 0.064 s** `[MODELLED]`. `F` is a
   dispatch/overhead floor — plausibly Python, tokenisation, MPS kernel launch, and the fixed
   prompt scaffold. At `n=61` the floor is 0.010 s against a measured 0.016 s, so the smallest
   cell is ~60 % overhead. The FLOP model predicts 31.5× from `n=61` to `n=1032`; the measurement
   is 13.2× — a 2.4× miss, entirely explained by `F`.
2. **`p = 1.80`, not 2.0.** The exact quadratic model (`p=2`) fits worse (RMSE 0.118 s vs 0.064 s).
   This is consistent with a real effect: at these sizes MPS attention is not yet in an
   asymptotic regime, and memory traffic grows faster than FLOPs.
3. **A constant-like scaling of per-token cost at the top end.** Measured per-token latency rises
   from 0.00020 s/token at `n=1032` to 0.00065 s/token at `n=6912` — a 3.2× rise for a 6.7× length
   increase. The pure model predicts a 6.7× rise; the measurement is 3.2×.

**What survives.** The model's *shape* is right and its asymptote is right: measured `n=8192`-limit
latency is well fit by a near-quadratic (local exponents 1.54–1.60 over `n ≥ 3972`), and the
8192/1024 ratio of 35.5× is the right order even though the correct number is closer to 8–20×
depending on how much of the ratio you attribute to the floor. **Use the model to predict
*direction and rank* between arms, never to predict an absolute ratio.** For anything absolute,
calibrate `F`, `a`, `p` on this box first — they are device-specific and the fits above are from
Apple MPS.

**Also note the direction of the introduced confound.** The upstream artifact's `limit=1024` column
is *truncated*, so its cost is flat while the `limit=8192` column's cost grows. The 17× headline gap
in `plan.md` §1 is therefore mostly the cost of not truncating, not the cost of attention — which is
exactly why an intervention that keeps the evidence without keeping all 7808 state tokens (H5's
premise) has a large cost headroom to work with. `[DERIVED]`.

## 4. Effective context — an operational definition

The phrase is useless unless it is (i) a property of the *prompt layout*, not of the encoder alone,
and (ii) defined by a sweep that can actually be run. Proposal:

> **Definition (EC@τ).** Fix a haystack of `L` tokens drawn from a frozen filler pool, a frozen
> question template whose `[MASK]` option markers land at position `m`, and a needle of length `ν`
> placed so that its **last** token is at absolute position `p`. Run the shipped model at
> `max_len ≥ L + head_len` and score the item. Choose `τ = 0.05` above the position-only oracle.
> Then
>
> ```
> EC(τ) = max { L : acc(L, p = m + L) >= acc_short - τ  and  p is not truncated }
> ```
>
> where `acc_short` is accuracy at the smallest `L` in the sweep with the *same relative needle
> placement*, and `acc(L, p)` is the accuracy over `N` items per cell.

Four design choices in that definition are load-bearing and should not be silently changed:

1. **The needle is placed by distance from the marker, `p = m + L`, not by fraction of the
   document.** Fraction-of-document placement confounds distance with document length, and
   `P1-mechanism.md` Control 2 shows those are separable effects. The lab's own `position-sweep`
   should record which convention it used.
2. **`acc_short` is a within-sweep reference, so `EC` measures *distance decay*, not absolute
   capability.** An absolute threshold cannot distinguish "this model cannot do the task" from
   "this model cannot do long context", and the two must not be reported as one number.
3. **`p is not truncated` is checked and reported per cell.** At `max_len=1024` the shipped state
   budget is `max_len - head_len - 1` = 1024 - 45 - 1 = 978 tokens for the shipped question (less
   for a longer head); above that the needle is simply absent,
   and the measurement is about truncation, not context. Every cell must record delivered token
   count alongside accuracy — the upstream artifact does this, and it is why §3.3 could normalize
   at all.
4. **`τ = 0.05` and `N` are chosen from the power argument in §5, not from convenience.** With
   `N = 200` and a within-cell paired comparison, a 0.05 difference is not resolvable at 80 %
   power in the high-discordance regime; `N = 400` resolves 0.10 comfortably and 0.05 only when the
   arms agree on ≥ 90 % of items.

**Reported form.** `EC(τ=0.05) = <L> tokens (95 % CI over a bootstrap of the item pool), at
max_len = <8192>, delivered = <L + head_len> tokens, head_len = 40, needle = <template id>`.
A single number with no `max_len`, no delivered length, and no item pool is not the definition and
should be rejected in review.

**Secondary, cheaper diagnostics that fit the same sweep** (each is a column, not a separate run):
the forced-choice probability of the gold option; the *rank* of the gold option among the four
(`ranks` degrade before `top-1` does and are less binomial-y); and the per-item agreement between
the frozen head and a probe on the marker representation, which is the quantity §2.4 says is
0.82-vs-0.30 and is the single most diagnostic number in the whole program.

## 5. Experiment grid, with the power argument

### 5.1 What actually needs measuring

Three separable quantities, in priority order:

| # | quantity | why it is needed | grid |
|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | **pilot**: within-cell variance, arm-to-arm discordance `q`, oracle/majority floors | §5.3 shows `q` is the only parameter that sets power; it is not known and must be estimated before the main run is sized | 8 cells, `N = 100`, cheap |
| S1 | **stage A** — upstream-compatible reconstruction: pad × `max_len` | reproduces 0.35-flat and the 17× cost, and establishes the truncation wall on this box | 8 pads × 2 limits |
| S2 | **stage B** — receptive-field/horizon sweep at fixed delivered length | separates distance from length (`P1-mechanism.md` Controls 1–2), and is the only grid that can distinguish the §1.1(A) and §1.1(B) mechanisms | 6 lengths × 5 positions |

**Stage A** (upstream-compatible). Pads `{0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000}`, limits
`{1024, 8192}`, needle embedded in the padded request so that its last token sits at the end of the
delivered sequence. Rationale: it is the only grid directly comparable to the artifact in §3.2, and
the `pad=1000↔2000` boundary is where the state budget is crossed (978 tokens) — the transition
from "reading badly" to "not there".

**Stage B** (the diagnostic that answers the issue). Sequence length
`n ∈ {512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 6144, 8192}` × needle position within the state block at
`d ∈ {64, 512, 2048, 4096, n - m - 1}` tokens from the marker. Always report the **delivered**
token count. Rationale: the `d = 64` cell is the positive control (inside the marker's own sliding
window, and it survives 4000 trailing tokens per `P1-mechanism.md`); `d = n - m - 1` is the
end-of-document case the failure was first seen at; the others straddle the `L*(d)` boundaries at
128 / 960 / 1984 / 4032 / 8128 from §1.1(B), which is what makes the two mechanisms separable. If
accuracy is flat within a band and drops at those boundaries, hop count binds; if it falls smoothly
in `n`, dilution binds.

**One item pool, shared across arms.** Both arms must be scored on the *same* items in the *same*
cell, or the comparison is unpaired and needs ~2.5× the `N` (§5.4). Generate `N` items per cell
(filler seed × needle template × label), never reuse a needle template across splits, and keep the
label distribution balanced so a constant answer cannot beat chance.

### 5.2 `N`, and the confidence interval the issue asks for

**Half-width of a 95 % CI for a single proportion near 0.5.** Wald `1.96·√(0.25/N)` versus the
exact Clopper–Pearson interval `[MODELLED] [DERIVED]`, computed in log space in `analyse.py` §5 and
self-checked against the published `CP(20, 7) = [0.1539, 0.5922]`:

| `N` | Wald half-width | exact CP interval at `x = N/2` | exact CP half-width |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 0.2193 | [0.2720, 0.7280] | 0.2280 |
| 200 | 0.0693 | [0.4287, 0.5713] | 0.0713 |
| 400 | 0.0490 | [0.4499, 0.5501] | 0.0501 |
| 600 | 0.0400 | [0.4592, 0.5408] | 0.0408 |
| 1200 | 0.0283 | — | — |

So **`N = 400` gives ±0.049 (Wald) / ±0.050 (exact) at `p̂ = 0.5`**, and ±0.040 exact at `N = 600`.
`plan.md` §6's "±0.066 at `N ≥ 200`" reproduces (0.0693 Wald) — it is the right number for a
*single proportion*, but it is **not** the resolution of an arm-vs-arm comparison, which is a paired
test. `[MODELLED]`.

**The exact-conditional caveat.** The *conditional* McNemar (sign) test — condition on the observed
number of discordant items, then `X ~ Bin(m, 1/2)` — is conservative: its rejection probability under
`H1` is at most `α` for every `m` below the point where the two-sided critical region is non-empty.
Measured in `analyse.py` §5, its power stays in 0.054–0.089 for every `(N, δ, q)` tried, out to
`N = 1600`. Do not size a design on it, and do not quote a p-value from it. `[MODELLED]`.

### 5.3 `N`, properly: power for the paired comparison

The right quantity is power of the **unconditional** McNemar test, and the parameter that sets it is
**`q = P(the two arms disagree on an item)`** — not `δ` alone. Exact unconditional power, computed by
summing the exact rejection region over two independent binomials (no normal approximation), with a
self-check of the rejection threshold against the normal value `z·SD` `[MODELLED]`:

| `q` | `δ = 0.05` @ N=200 | @ N=400 | @ N=600 | @ N=800 | `δ = 0.10` @ N=400 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.10 | 0.540 | 0.891 | 0.975 | 0.996 | 1.000 |
| 0.20 | 0.337 | 0.616 | **0.821** | 0.903 | 0.997 |
| 0.30 | 0.264 | 0.480 | 0.672 | 0.790 | 0.975 |
| 0.50 | 0.194 | 0.357 | 0.513 | 0.625 | 0.899 |

Cross-checked against the standard normal-approximation sample-size formula
`N = (z_{α/2}√q + z_β√(q − δ²))² / δ²`, which is accurate to ≈ 0.01 in this range and gives the
familiar design numbers: **`N = 312` for `δ=0.05, q=0.10`; `N = 626` for `q=0.20`; `N = 1568` for
`q=0.50`; and `N = 77 / 155 / 391` for `δ=0.10` at `q = 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.50`.** `[MODELLED]`.

**Recommended `N = 400` per cell.** Justification, stated as what it does and does not buy:

- For the decision rules actually written down (`plan.md` §4: H1 needs `≥ 0.20`, H2 `≥ 0.10`,
  H3 `≥ 0.05`, H5 `≥ 0.05`), `N = 400` has **`≥ 0.90` power at `δ = 0.10` for every `q ≤ 0.50`**,
  and `≥ 0.97` at `q ≤ 0.30`. H1 and H2 are therefore well powered.
- **H3 and H5 at `δ = 0.05` are NOT powered at `N = 400`**: power is 0.89 at `q = 0.10`, 0.62 at
  `q = 0.20`, 0.48 at `q = 0.30`. A null result on a `+0.05` arm at `N = 400` is uninterpretable and
  must be reported as *underpowered*, not as *no effect*. Detectable differences at `N = 400` are
  roughly `δ = 0.05` at `q ≤ 0.10` and `δ = 0.10` at `q ≤ 0.30`.
- `N = 400` also keeps the per-cell resolution useful: one item = 0.0025 accuracy, and a
  majority-class floor of ~0.35 is exactly 140/400.
- **The pilot (S0) is not optional.** `q` is the only free parameter and it is unknown; it must be
  estimated from ~100 items in the cells that matter (the tail cells, `d ≥ 2048`) before the main
  run is sized, and the realized `q` reported with every comparison. If `q` comes back at 0.3 in the
  tail cells, `δ = 0.05` is not testable at any affordable `N` and the plan should say so up front.

### 5.4 Multiplicity

The full grid is 8×2 + 6×5 = **46 cells**. With `m` comparisons at `α = 0.05` and all nulls true,
`P(≥ 1 false positive)` is **0.72 at `m = 25`** and **0.92 at `m = 50`**; Bonferroni
`α = 0.05/m` inflates the required `N` by `(z_{1-α/2m}/z_{1-α/2})²` = **2.49× at `m = 25`** and
**2.82× at `m = 50`** `[MODELLED]`. Consequences for the design:

- Do **not** Holm-correct all 46 cells at `N = 400`; that turns every `δ = 0.05` comparison into an
  automatic failure.
- Instead, pre-register a **small primary family** (the `d ∈ {64, 2048, 4096, end}` cells at
  `n ∈ {2048, 8192}`, say 8 comparisons) and treat the rest as exploratory, reported with CIs and
  explicitly labelled exploratory. State the primary family in `protocol.md` **before** the run.
- Use **McNemar on item-paired predictions**, not two independent proportions, and use **Holm
  within the primary family only**.

### 5.5 Cost, `[MODELLED]` from the fitted latency

From `lat(n) = 0.010 + 5.575e-07·n^1.800` (§3.3) — so these are the *upstream MPS* rates, and a CUDA
run on this box should be cheaper. The two artifacts give a rough cross-device multiplier:
at pad=4000, limit=8192 the upstream MPS run took 1.707 s and `P1-mechanism.md`'s CUDA bf16 run
took 0.230 s — **7.4×**, `[DERIVED]` from two `[MEASURED]` numbers on different devices and
therefore indicative only, since the inputs and the prompt layout are not identical:

| grid | cells | `N` | forwards / arm | modelled h/arm (MPS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 pilot | 8 | 100 | 800 | 0.4 |
| S1 stage A | 16 | 400 | 6,400 | 3.2 |
| S2 stage B | 30 | 400 | 12,000 | 13.8 |
| S1+S2, 2 arms | 46 | 400 | 36,800 | 17.0 |
| S1+S2, 4 arms (baseline + H1 + H2 + H3) | 46 | 400 | 73,600 | 33.9 |

One GPU, `flock`-serialised per `AGENTS.md`. Applying the indicative 7.4× cross-device multiplier
to the MPS column, S1+S2 with 2 arms is ≈ 2.3 h and 4 arms ≈ 4.6 h on this box's 4070 — affordable,
which is the main argument for `N = 400` over `N = 200`. Treat those two figures as `[MODELLED]`
with a device-transfer assumption attached, not as a measurement; the MPS column above is the
direct `[MODELLED]` output. The 46-cell × 400 × 4-arm grid is the expensive corner; stage it, and
spend the extra `N` only on the primary family.

## 6. Assumptions ranked by how much they would hurt if wrong

1. **The FLOP model is proportional to latency.** Demonstrably false at small `n` (§3.3), partly
   false at large `n`. Used here only for ratios, always tagged `[MODELLED]`.
2. **The per-hop horizon (§1.1(B)) is the right quantitative model of information transfer.**
   It is a hop-count, and the evidence says the binding constraint is softmax dilution. Use it for
   horizon and rank, never for recovery probability.
3. **Layer-0 full attention is not itself the fix.** It makes every token a depth-1 ancestor, but a
   depth-1 ancestor read by a raw-embedding query is nearly unweighted evidence. §2.4's 0.82-vs-0.30
   is the empirical statement of this; §1.1(A) alone does not establish that the head is at fault,
   only that reachability is not the limit.
4. **`render_options` reads `q["crit"]`.** Probed: with `"criteria"` the options render empty. Any
   grid built from the artifact JSON must rename the key, or the head block silently shrinks and the
   marker positions move.
5. **The upstream latency artifact is an Apple MPS measurement.** §3.3's `F`, `a`, `p` are
   device-specific and must not be transplanted to CUDA without re-fitting.
6. **Nothing here has been independently verified.** This file is a derivation plus a design.
   The interval and power tables are reproducible by one command; the mechanism reading in §2.4
   depends on `P1b`, which is itself still `candidate`.

## 7. What would falsify this document

| claim | falsifier |
|---|---|
| Reachability graph has diameter 1 | a per-layer attention-mass map showing the marker's layer-0 attention is effectively zero on distant keys **and** that no later path recovers them — would make §1.1(A) vacuous in practice and restore hop count as the binding constraint |
| Distance costs via dilution, not hop count | accuracy flat within `L*(d)` bands and stepping at 129/961/1985/4033/8129 in a controlled sweep |
| FLOP model misses the measured ratio | a re-fit on CUDA landing within, say, 20 % of the measured 8192/1024 ratio — that would mean the miss in §3.3 was MPS-specific overhead, not a model failure |
| `N = 400` powers `δ = 0.10` | a pilot `q > 0.5` in the tail cells, which would push `δ = 0.10` out of reach as well |
